nomination.name: Christian author David Clark
nomination.summary: Christian author David M. Clark says standing at his father’s graveside forced him to confront what real gratitude means. He argues that thankfulness rooted only in good circumstances is fragile, calling it merely “relief,” while biblical gratitude is grounded in who God is even in grief, loss and suffering. Clark warns against what he calls “Me-ology,” a self-centered version of faith that asks what God can do for us instead of worshiping Him for who He is. Drawing on Scripture, he says Christ

nomination.name: Ephesians 2:20 Paul God
nomination.summary: And that’s where Ephesians 2:20 becomes important to me. Paul says the household of God is “built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone.” I understand the foundation as something laid, not something continually relaid. I also agree with you that the Church needs order, leadership, teaching, and accountability. I don’t believe Christianity means every individual simply follows whatever they personally feel the Spirit is telling them.

nomination.name: Scriptures God God Christ
nomination.summary: The Scriptures tell us who God is, and they reveal our fallen condition. They announce God's covenant promises, and they proclaim Christ's incarnation, death, resurrection, ascension, and coming judgment. They teach us the way of repentance and faith, and, above all, they bear witness to Jesus Christ. This is why the Anglican formularies refuse to treat Scripture as an optional supplement to Christian life. Article VI does not say merely that Scripture contains some helpful things about salvati

nomination.name: Finally Scripture God
nomination.summary: Finally, Scripture is profitable “for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.” In the King James Bible the word is “throughly,” indicating equipment running through the entire man, not a little religious polish smeared across the surface. God intends Scripture to furnish the believer for service. The Bible supplies truth for witnessing, wisdom for decisions, comfort for suffering, answers for error, standards for conduct, warning
